test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A train goes from P to Q at a speed of 20 km/h. Then it goes from Q to R at a speed of q km/h. Finally the train goes from R to S at a speed of r km/h. The distances from P to Q, Q to R and R to S are equal. If the average speed from P to R is (280)/(11) km/h, and the average speed from Q to S is (112)/(3) km/h, then what is the value of r ?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of train goes from P to Q = 20 km/h

Speed of train goes from Q to R = q km/h

Speed of train goes from R to S = r km/h

Average speed from P to R = (280)/(11) km/h

Average speed from Q to S = (112)/(3) km/h

**Calculations:**

Let the distance between P to Q be d.

QR = d

RS = d

Average speed = total distance/total time

Total time = distance/speed

Time taken by train from P to Q = d/20 -------------(1)

Time taken by train from Q to S

= 2d/(112/3)

= 3d/56

Time taken by train from P to R = 2d/(280/11) ---------(2)

Time taken by train from Q to R

From Eqⁿ(2) - Eqⁿ(1)

= 2d/(280/11) - d/20

= 11d/140 - d/20

= 11d/140 - 7d/140

= 4d/140

= d/35

Total time by train from R to S = Time taken from Q to S - Time taken from Q to R

= 3d/56 - d/35

= 49d/1960

= d/40

Now, According to question,

Time is taken by train from R to S:

d/r = d/40 

⇒ r = 40 km/h

**Hence, The Required value of r = 40 km/h.**
